name: iwopy
raw_meta_yaml:
{% set name = "iwopy" %}
{% set version = "1.0.0" %}

package:
  name: {{ name|lower }}
  version: {{ version }}

source:
  url: https://github.com/FraunhoferIWES/iwopy/archive/v{{ version }}.tar.gz
  sha256: db198670a6451b4582387eeda12a39f28053336665e00eedd61ea84a160ef115

build:
  noarch: python
  script: {{ PYTHON }} -m pip install . -vv --no-deps --no-build-isolation
  number: 0

requirements:
  host:
    - python {{ python_min }}
    - pip
    - setuptools >=84.0.0
    - wheel >=0.46.2
  run:
    - python >={{ python_min }}
    - matplotlib-base >=3.8
    - numpy >=1.26
    - scipy >=1.12

test:
  imports:
    - iwopy
  requires:
    - python {{ python_min }}
    - pip
    - pytest >=9.0.3
    - pyyaml
    - tomli >=2
    - pymoo >=0.6
    - pygmo >=2.19
    - optuna >=5.0.0
    - deap >=1.4.4
  source_files:
    - tests
    - examples
    - notebooks
    - pyproject.toml
    - CHANGELOG.md
    - CITATION.cff
    - .github/workflows/test.yml
    - .github/workflows/publish.yml
    - iwopy/benchmarks/quadratic.py
    - iwopy/interfaces/pymoo/factory.py
    - iwopy/interfaces/pygmo/algos.py
  commands:
    - pip check
    - pytest tests -q -k "not cma and not nevergrad"

about:
  home: https://github.com/FraunhoferIWES/iwopy
  summary: Fraunhofer IWES optimization tools in Python
  description: |
    The iwopy package is a meta package that provides interfaces to
    other open-source Python optimization packages out there. It can
    thus be understood as an attempt to provide the best of all worlds
    when it comes to solving optimization problems with Python. All
    the credit for implementing the invoked optimizers goes to the
    original package providers.
  license: MIT
  license_file: LICENSE

extra:
  recipe-maintainers:
    - SchmJo
